name: Colac
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Blake, Clark & Reid 1998, The Colac language (in Blake ed., Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria, Pacific Linguistics) — not online

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 page for cola1237 'Colac' (references: Blake 2011 subclassification comment; Campbell et al. 2022 AES; Blake, Clark & Reid 1998; Hercus 1969; Bowern 2011).
sources.note: Bibliographic page only; alternative names Coligan, Kolacgnat, Kolakngat, Kolijon, Caligun, Koladgin, Koligian; WALS clc; extinct.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. & Julie Reid. 1998. Classifying Victorian languages. In Blake (ed.) 1998, 1-58. Pacific Linguistics C-147.
sources.note: Colac appears only for its location (p.4) and in lexicostatistic tables; the volume's only stress remarks (p.5; p.13 fn.11: 'Although in most Australian languages the stress is on the first syllable, in Madi-Madi.. the stress was on the second syllable') concern Madhi-Madhi, not Colac.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J., Ian Clark & Julie Reid. 1998. The Colac language. In Barry J. Blake (ed.), Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria, 155-177. Pacific Linguistics C-147. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C147.155 (online edition 2015, CC BY-SA 4.0).
sources.note: Sec. 2 Phonology, pp.160-163 (2.1 phoneme inventory: consonants, vowels; 2.2 phonotactics; consonant clusters) contains no word-stress or accent statement; 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the chapter. p.160: 'we have few tokens for most items and consequently more than usual difficulty in working out the pronunciation.' The description is reconstituted from five 19th-c. word lists (Tuckfield 1844 / Cary 1898, Dennis 1878, Lloyd 1862, Robinson MSS).
sources.venue: Wathawurrung and the Colac language of southern Victoria

sources.citation: Smyth, R. Brough. 1878. The Aborigines of Victoria, vol. 2, p.89: 'Colac' vocabulary (W. & A. Dennis).
sources.note: 48-word English-Colac list only; no phonetic notes.
Only features 129A and 130A (hand/arm, finger/hand) coded; no stress features 14A-17A.

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. 2011. Dialects of Western Kulin; Blake, Hercus, Morey & Ryan 2011. The Mathi group of languages (PL 628); Blake 2003. The Warrnambool language (PL 544); Blake 2003. The Bunganditj language (PL 549).
sources.note: Colac occurs only in lexicostatistic tables and cognate notes (a full-text search for stress/accent Colac/Gulidjan); no Colac stress statement in any of them.
sources.venue: The Mathi group of languages (PL 628); Blake

sources.citation: Blake, Barry J. 2011. Kulin and its neighbours. La Trobe University ms. (VCAA-hosted PDF).
sources.note: Colac data limited to Table 16 pronouns (p.27) and lexical comparisons (Table 28); only stress remark is fn.13 p.19 'Unfortunately old sources do not notate stress.' (context: Lower Murray languages), nothing on Colac stress.

sources.citation: Bowern, Claire. 2011. How many languages were spoken in Australia? [Austlangs master language list spreadsheet] (Glottolog 5.1's only reference for cola1237).
sources.note: One row: Kolakngat, Pama-Nyungan, subgroup Kulin, AIATSIS S30, no ISO code. A list of languages, not a description; nothing on stress.
sources.venue: [Austlangs master language list spreadsheet] (Glottolog 5.1's only reference for cola1237)

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gulidjan language' (cites AIATSIS S30, Blake, Clark & Reid 1998, Dixon 2002).
sources.note: No phonology; notes c.100 words attested, possibly a mixed language with elements of neighbouring languages.

sources.citation: Hercus, Luise A. 1986. Victorian languages: a late survey. Pacific Linguistics B-77. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Colac/Gulidjan not covered (Cary 1898 appears only in the bibliography); her initial-stress statements concern the Kulin languages she recorded (Wemba-Wemba, Wergaia, Woiwurrung etc.), not Colac.

sources.citation: Cary, John J. 1898. Vocabularies of the Geelong and Colac tribes, collected in 1840 [from Francis Tuckfield's MSS; 'Kolijon' = Colac]. Report of the 7th meeting of the Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science (Sydney) 7: 840-872.
sources.note: 'Letters' (p.847) and 'Sounds' (p.848): Tuckfield's marked vowels give long/short vowel values only, plus a note on the 'gn' nasal; no accent or stress statement for Kolijon or the other dialects.
sources.venue: Report of the 7th meeting of the Australasian Association for the Advancement of Science (Sydney)

sources.citation: Lloyd, G. T. 1862. Thirty-three years in Tasmania and Victoria. London: Houlston & Wright (Colac/Wathawurrung word list, pp.470-471).
sources.note: One of the five sources of Blake et al. 1998; 70-word mixed Colac/Wathawurrung list; a memoir, not expected to state accent; open scans exist on archive.org / Google Books but were not downloaded.

sources.citation: Dixon, R. M. W. 2002. Australian languages: their nature and development. Cambridge: CUP (treats Colac as a possible mixed language).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative/historical survey cited by Wikipedia for the classification; Dixon's stress discussion is general, and he had no Colac data beyond Blake et al. 1998, so no Colac-specific statement is expected.

sources.citation: Hercus, Luise A. 1969. The languages of Victoria: a late survey, 2 vols. Canberra: AIAS (first edition of Hercus 1986, listed by Glottolog for cola1237).

sources.note: Glottolog lists it for Colac, but the 1986 edition held by the project does not cover Colac (the language was extinct before Hercus's fieldwork); expected to be equally silent.
